1: # SurgeIndex
2: 
3: SurgeIndex is a production-minded MVP for discovering websites that are gaining attention. The public experience is a warm, fast directory with live-style rankings, breakout signals, explainable Heat Scores, source-aware metrics, claim flow, referral tracking, and a clearly separated sponsored distribution lane.
4: 
5: The repository is intentionally runnable in `APP_MODE=demo` with `DATA_PROVIDER=demo`: the public app has deterministic fictional sites so the product can be reviewed without database, GA4, Tinybird, Stripe, or Cloudflare credentials. The production path requires `APP_MODE=production`, `DATA_PROVIDER=postgres`, a database, and a Better Auth secret. There is no silent fallback between modes or providers.
6: 
7: ## Quick start
8: 
9: Requirements: Node.js 20.9+, pnpm 11, and Docker only if you want local Postgres.
10: 
11: ```bash
12: pnpm install
13: cp .env.example apps/web/.env
14: pnpm dev
15: ```
16: 
17: Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Demo mode is enabled in the example environment. No database is required for the public review flow.
18: 
19: Useful commands:
20: 
21: ```bash
22: pnpm typecheck       # all workspace packages
23: pnpm lint            # Next/React lint
24: pnpm test            # Vitest unit and contract tests
25: pnpm test:e2e        # Playwright Chromium flow tests; starts port 3100
26: pnpm build           # tracker bundle, then Next production build
27: pnpm start           # serve the Next production build
28: pnpm db:up           # optional local Postgres
29: pnpm tracker:build   # rebuild apps/web/public/tracker.js
30: pnpm traffic:load    # bounded local/staging collector correctness probe
31: pnpm ga4:fixture     # deterministic read-only GA4 provider smoke test
32: pnpm ga4:sync        # production Postgres Core sync; demo mode exits disabled
33: pnpm ga4:realtime    # production Postgres Realtime sync; demo mode exits disabled
34: pnpm ga4:backfill    # production Postgres bounded backfill; demo mode exits disabled
35: pnpm ga4:health      # production Postgres GA4 operations view; demo mode exits disabled
36: pnpm boost:fixture   # deterministic Boost delivery/reporting fixture; never charges
37: pnpm boost:forecast  # production inventory forecast; demo mode exits disabled
38: pnpm boost:pace      # idempotent pacing job seam; demo mode exits disabled
39: pnpm boost:aggregate # rebuild persisted delivery aggregates; demo mode exits disabled
40: pnpm boost:reconcile-payments # inspect pending application payment ledger rows
41: pnpm boost:release-reservations # release expired Checkout inventory holds
42: pnpm stripe:test-webhook # local signed Stripe fixture only; no network or charge
43: pnpm launch:gates   # report tracker, GA4, Stripe, and each Boost placement gate
44: pnpm launch:check   # complete deterministic release check; requires an explicit disposable DB for migration smoke
45: pnpm db:smoke       # fresh + 0011 upgrade migration smoke; requires disposable DB/reset opt-in
46: pnpm production:import -- --file sites.csv # dry-run real-site metadata import; add guarded --apply only after review
47: pnpm preview         # OpenNext Cloudflare preview; requires adapter setup
48: pnpm deploy          # OpenNext Cloudflare deploy; requires Cloudflare auth
49: ```
50: 
51: The root `pnpm build` also copies the minified first-party tracker to `apps/web/public/tracker.js`.
52: 
53: ## Product surface
54: 
55: The public experience includes:
56: 
57: - Homepage with a live-style hero chart, query/category filters, Live/24H/7D/Breakouts/New tabs, ranked cards, source badges, and activity strip.
58: - `/rankings`, `/breakouts`, `/categories`, `/categories/[slug]`, `/search`, and `/site/[slug]` directory surfaces.
59: - Site profiles with Heat Score breakdown, rank history, attention chart, referral count, verification state, related sites, and a secure `/go/[siteSlug]` referral redirect.
60: - `/live` and `/api/live/[siteId]` report accepted tracker active visitors/sessions with local or explicitly configured Durable Object realtime.
61: - `/submit` domain validation and waitlist-ready submission flow, plus ownership verification architecture at `/claim/[siteId]`.
62: - `/methodology`, `/pricing`, `/boost`, `/creators`, `/campaigns`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, and a custom not-found page.
63: - Demo owner workspace at `/dashboard`, with sites, analytics, verification, badge, boosts, billing, and settings surfaces.
64: - Production owner tracker installation and analytics at `/dashboard/sites/[siteId]/verification` and `/dashboard/sites/[siteId]/analytics`.
65: - Development-only real tracker fixture at `/dev/tracker-fixture` and aggregate operational summary at `/admin/traffic`.
66: - Demo admin review queue at `/admin`.
67: - JSON endpoints for leaderboard, categories, activity, search, site detail, time series, site submission, event collection, and SVG badges.
68: 
69: ## Architecture
70: 
71: ```mermaid
72: flowchart LR
73:   Browser[Public web + owner dashboard] --> Next[Next.js App Router]
74:   Browser --> Tracker[First-party tracker.js]
75:   Next --> API[Route handlers]
76:   Tracker --> Collector[Local or Cloudflare collector]
77:   Collector --> Queue[Local adapter or Cloudflare Queue]
78:   Queue --> Consumer[Queue consumer]
79:   Consumer --> Analytics[Postgres or Tinybird provider]
80:   Analytics --> Aggregates[Current metrics + hourly snapshots]
81:   Next --> Aggregates
82:   Collector --> Realtime[Local registry or site Durable Object]
83:   Realtime --> Browser
84: ```
85: 
86: The package boundaries are:
87: 
88: - `packages/shared`: types, URL/domain safety, formatting, source labels, and shared utilities.
89: - `packages/scoring`: deterministic Heat Score v1, small-base protection, explainable breakdowns, and rank comparator.
90: - `packages/anti-fraud`: tracker event and outbound click validation, replay/heartbeat checks, and fraud penalties.
91: - `packages/analytics`: shared event-store/provider interfaces, deterministic demo provider, Postgres event store, and Tinybird adapter.
92: - `packages/ga4`: normalized read-only Google Analytics 4 OAuth/provider contracts, deterministic fixture provider, domain matching, report normalization, and retry helpers.
93: - `packages/db`: Drizzle schema covering identity, sites, claims, verification, current/snapshot traffic metrics, tracker keys/events, attribution, ingestion failures, active sessions, ranks, boosts, payments, fraud flags, and moderation.
94: - `tracker`: consent-aware first-party tracker bundle with one-time initialization, SPA navigation, visibility/engagement, retry, attribution cleanup, and measured bundle output.
95: - `workers/collector`, `workers/queue-consumer`, `workers/realtime`, `workers/aggregation`: Cloudflare Worker implementations for ingestion, asynchronous processing, site-level live fan-out, and scheduled aggregation.
96: 
97: ## Truth and trust rules
98: 
99: Every metric in the review experience carries a source label. Fictional values are labeled `Demo Data`; connected-source labels are reserved for real tracker or GA4 measurements. The public cards distinguish traffic from SurgeIndex referrals, and the boost experience explicitly states that paid placement never changes organic rank or Heat Score.

3: `surgeindex-tracker.php` is a narrowly scoped must-use WordPress plugin for
4: `higuppy.com`. It keeps SurgeIndex outside the dirty child-theme and custom

7:

9: - `surgeindex_site_key`: the 32-character suffix `pk_live_...` public tracker key.

12: with owner `www:www` and mode `0644`. Before replacement, preserve the remote
13: file (if any), verify the expected pre-change hash, lint with the PHP 8.3 CLI,
14: purge the WordPress/FastCGI cache, and compare the remote SHA-256 with this
15: source.

17: The integration reads the existing `window.higuppyGa4` consent API. SurgeIndex
18: is not loaded until HiGuppy analytics consent is `granted`; deny/reset stops the
19: tracker and grant clears the opt-out before resuming it on the same page. The
20: server-side route gate keeps the script off account, checkout, order, password

22: tracker also replaces identifier-like pathname segments with `:id` before an
23: event is serialized. It sends only anonymous traffic metadata documented in the
24: plugin header, never WooCommerce cart, order, account, form, or page-content
25: data.

30: aggregate to SurgeIndex. Cancelled and on-hold orders are deliberately
31: excluded. The bridge sends no order IDs, customer information, or credentials;
32: the VPS systemd timer supplies the private `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`.

1: # Backup and restore runbook
2: 
3: ## Design
4: 
5: The primary backup is a PostgreSQL custom-format dump created by
6: `deploy/vps/surgeindex-postgres-backup`. It is written atomically under
7: `/var/backups/surgeindex/postgres` and retained locally for 14 days.
8: 
9: The offsite script creates a fresh dump from the `surgeindex-db` container,
10: encrypts it with age before it leaves the host, uploads the `.dump.age` object
11: to the configured S3-compatible destination, and retains a short local staging
12: window. The verification script downloads the latest encrypted object,
13: decrypts it with a root-only identity, and runs `pg_restore --list` without
14: connecting to a live database.
15: 
16: No dump, age private key, S3 credential, or provider token belongs in Git.
17: 
18: ## Install on the VPS
19: 
20: Install scripts as root-owned mode `0750` under `/usr/local/sbin` and install
21: these units under `/etc/systemd/system`:
22: 
23: - `surgeindex-postgres-backup.service` / `.timer`
24: - `surgeindex-postgres-backup-offsite.service` / `.timer`
25: - `surgeindex-postgres-backup-verify.service` / `.timer`
26: 
27: Create `/etc/surgeindex/backup.env` from
28: `deploy/vps/surgeindex-backup.env.example`, populate it through the host secret
29: manager, and set mode `0600`. Store the age identity at the path named by
30: `BACKUP_AGE_IDENTITY_FILE`, also mode `0600`, readable only by root. Confirm
31: the age recipient and identity correspond before enabling the timer.
32: 
33: ```bash
34: sudo install -o root -g root -m 0750 deploy/vps/surgeindex-postgres-backup /usr/local/sbin/
35: sudo install -o root -g root -m 0750 deploy/vps/surgeindex-postgres-backup-offsite /usr/local/sbin/
36: sudo install -o root -g root -m 0750 deploy/vps/surgeindex-postgres-backup-verify /usr/local/sbin/
37: sudo systemctl daemon-reload
38: sudo systemctl enable --now surgeindex-postgres-backup.timer
39: sudo systemctl enable --now surgeindex-postgres-backup-offsite.timer
40: sudo systemctl enable --now surgeindex-postgres-backup-verify.timer
41: ```
42: 
43: The backup services require Docker, `pg_dump`/`pg_restore`, `age`, and the AWS
44: CLI (or compatible S3 CLI) to be installed on the host. Verify the journal
45: after the first run:
46: 
47: ```bash
48: sudo systemctl start surgeindex-postgres-backup.service
49: sudo journalctl -u surgeindex-postgres-backup.service -n 100 --no-pager
50: sudo systemctl start surgeindex-postgres-backup-offsite.service
51: sudo journalctl -u surgeindex-postgres-backup-offsite.service -n 100 --no-pager
52: sudo systemctl start surgeindex-postgres-backup-verify.service
53: sudo journalctl -u surgeindex-postgres-backup-verify.service -n 100 --no-pager
54: ```
55: 
56: Do not accept the backup as valid until the dump is non-zero, the offsite
57: upload succeeds, and verification reports `pg_restore --list` success.
58: 
59: ## Deterministic disposable restore drill
60: 
61: The restore target must be a newly created, disposable database with a name
62: that is not production/live-named. Never point this command at the live
63: database or the production volume.
64:

3: ## Request and identity boundaries
4: 
5: - `requestId()` accepts a bounded, safe caller ID or generates a UUID. JSON
6:   success and error responses return it in the body/header where applicable.
7: - Mutation routes use `assertSameOrigin()` and server-side Better Auth/session
8:   authorization. Admin routes use `requireApiAdmin()`; owner/editor routes
9:   check the site-owner relation server-side.
10: - `X-Forwarded-For` is never trusted by application code. The single shared
11:   `getTrustedClientIp()` implementation accepts a validated `X-Real-IP` only
12:   when an explicit proxy mode is configured; otherwise it returns `unknown`.
13: - Supplied Nginx vhosts overwrite X-Real-IP and clear XFF. The Cloudflare mode
14:   is documented as requiring an allowlist of current Cloudflare CIDRs before
15:   it may be enabled.
16: - Production rate limiting uses an atomic Postgres bucket keyed by a
17:   deployment-local SHA-256 digest; raw IPs and caller identifiers are not
18:   persisted. The process-local
19:   Map remains only for demo/development/test, where it is an intentional test
20:   adapter. Nginx adds a separate anonymous request limit to auth, submission,
21:   claim, waitlist, and tracker collection paths.
22: 
23: ## SSRF and outbound fetch
24: 
25: The public metadata/claim fetcher now:
26: 
27: - resolves every A/AAAA answer and rejects any mixed private/public answer;
28: - blocks loopback, private, link-local, metadata, multicast, unspecified,
29:   documentation, carrier-grade, reserved, and mapped-private IPv4/IPv6 ranges;
30: - connects to the just-validated address while retaining Host and TLS SNI;
31: - follows redirects manually, re-resolves every hop, caps redirects, rejects
32:   credential-bearing URLs and HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade;
33: - caps connection/total time, response bytes, and HTML content types; and
34: - fails closed when DNS, fetch, content, or metadata parsing is unsafe.
35: 
36: The SSRF fixture suite covers mixed answers, IPv4/IPv6 private ranges,
37: redirect-to-private, downgrade, pinned address/rebinding seam, content type,
38: declared and streamed response size, and a stalled response timeout. A real
39: network staging test remains separate evidence.

42: 
43: - Signup, submission, waitlist, claim start/verify, owner settings, password
44:   recovery, and verification resend have server-side Turnstile hooks or are
45:   authenticated. Production configuration fails closed unless Turnstile is
46:   explicitly enabled and provisioned; checks cover success, expected action,
47:   and optional exact hostname. Tokens are never logged or stored.
48: - Better Auth requires email verification in production. Password reset,
49:   verification resend, expiry/used-token handling, and transactional email
50:   callbacks are configured. Email delivery is an abstraction with disabled,
51:   console, and HTTP provider modes; production rejects disabled/console modes.
52: - Auth actions have durable rate limits and same-origin checks. The browser
53:   receives no provider credentials. The shared client-IP suite proves that
54:   changing X-Forwarded-For does not create a new limiter identity.

61:   being treated as verified.
